newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nordic nations back gas in sustainable energy pact.
newsitem.headline: Nordic nations back gas in sustainable energy pact.

text.p: The prime ministers of the five Nordic countries on Friday adopted a declaration on sustainable energy, backing natural gas, an integrated Baltic gas network and renewable energy such as solar and wave power.
The premiers have asked their energy ministers to investigate building pipelines and other infrastructure to form an integrated Nordic gas and electricity network.
They also said they wanted to see Russian gas brought into a system of European energy supplies.
"This is a historic declaration," Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland told a news conference on the final day of a two-day Nordic prime ministers' meeting here.
"This is the first time we have expressed a joint desire for a sustainable energy system around the Baltic Sea," he said.
In the declaration, the prime ministers said that natural gas was the most environmentally-friendly fossil fuel.

"We agree that the security of supplies will be enhanced and the environment will profit by national energy systems being integrated," the declaration added, noting that such a process was already underway in the electricity market.
"We note there are local gas networks which could serve as the basis for a wider Nordic and Baltic gas network," it said.
The prime ministers said the European Union was also interested in the development of a Nordic gas grid as part of an integrated European energy strategy.
"A vision for an integrated energy system may be realised," Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrupp Rasmussen said.

The prime ministers asked their energy ministers to assess the conditions for increased use of renewable energy and building the infrastructure for an integrated energy network and report on these issues at a November Nordic council meeting.

They also want the ministers to look at how duties can be harmonised, so that renewable sources of energy and gas can be commercially viable and reflect the environmental aspect of different sources of energy.
The ministers must also look at the role of international finance and borrowing for a gas network and make contact with other countries in the Baltic region. 291526 GMT jun 97
